instruction_given_to_self: SEPARATE authoring pass, explicit spurious mindset. Reading the same 60-row disagreement slice, name 10 features that are plausibly PREDICTIVE but are NOT quality: length/format proxies, boilerplate phrases, venue/community style markers, topic markers, temporal tells. These become DECLARED NUISANCES and never join the A bank. Label-blind: `judgement` was never loaded; no criterion references acceptance or any outcome.
scale: 0-10 integer, NA if the abstract gives no evidence bearing on the criterion

criteria.name: Anonymized-repository or release-on-acceptance code boilerplate
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 by how prominently the abstract carries submission-time artifact boilerplate: an anonymised repository link (for example an anonymous code-hosting URL or a placeholder), or a promise that code or data will be released later or upon publication. Score 0 when no such statement appears; score by presence and prominence of the boilerplate, not by whether sharing is a good practice.
criteria.rationale: Anonymised links appear verbatim in DL30, DL31, DL32, DL36, DL37, DL40, DL41; 'will be open-sourced upon acceptance' / 'will be publicly available' in DL39, DL45, DL46, DL52. It is a review-cycle and venue-policy artefact, and the Layer-1 SHAP screen already flagged v_kw_code x the availability-statement rubric as the top redundancy pair in this cell -- exactly the channel this feature isolates.

criteria.name: Abstract length and verbosity
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how long and densely packed the abstract is compared with a typical conference abstract: 0 for a very short abstract of a few sentences, 10 for one that runs long with many clauses and sub-points. Judge extent only; do not judge whether the length is warranted.
criteria.rationale: The classic length proxy. Length varies sharply across the slice (DH15, DH20, DL49 and DL57 are short; DH08, DH10, DL54 and DL37 are long) and it is already a V feature (v_char_len, v_word_len), so a judged version lets the discount be applied on the same footing as the mined B-features.

criteria.name: Enumerated list formatting inside the abstract
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract is organised as an explicit enumerated list — numbered or parenthesised items, 'First/Second/Finally' scaffolding, bulleted contributions. Score the formatting only, regardless of what the items say.
criteria.rationale: A pure format proxy. DH00 ('1) ... 2) ... 3) ...'), DH10 ('(1) ... (2) ... (3)'), DH17 and DL39 ('Firstly ... Secondly') use it heavily; most others do not. Formatting conventions travel with subcommunity and submission era.

criteria.name: Raw LaTeX or markup residue left in the abstract
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much unrendered markup survives in the abstract text: LaTeX commands, math delimiters left as literal characters, escaped percent or backslash characters, footnote markers, markdown emphasis. Score the residue only, not the content it decorates.
criteria.rationale: DL31 ('$N$', '$\leq$', '81.88\%'), DL39 ('38.9\%', '$5\times$', '\footnote{}'), DL40 ('\textsf{S}em\textsf{A}ntic', '\url{}'), DL50 ('384\%'), DH12 ('\textit{e.g.,}') and DH23 ('17.5$\times$') carry it. This is an ingestion and preprint-pipeline artefact — a temporal/format tell with no bearing on the work.

criteria.name: Topic sits in a currently dominant research area
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how central the abstract's subject is to the areas that currently dominate machine-learning publishing — large language models, multimodal or vision-language models, diffusion and other generative models, agents. Score topic membership only; a careful paper on an unfashionable topic should score low here.
criteria.rationale: A topic marker in the prereg's sense. The dense-high side is thick with LLM/MLLM/diffusion work (DH02, DH03, DH04, DH05, DH08, DH10, DH23, DH24, DH28) while the dense-low side carries more classical ML (DL31 random forests, DL43 SGD/DRO, DL48 label propagation, DL49 momentum, DL51 binary networks, DL55 spectral clustering). Topic prevalence is a property of the field's fashion cycle, not of the work.

criteria.name: Branded method name or acronym
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how strongly the work brands itself with a coined capitalised name or acronym for its method, system, dataset, or benchmark, and repeats that name through the abstract. Score the branding practice only.
criteria.rationale: HyperHuman/HumanVerse (DH00), LLaVA-Plus (DH02), COMM (DH04), JudgeLM (DH05), DSG (DH06), CUBE-LLM/LV3D (DH10), REPA (DH23), BGRL (DH17) versus unbranded work such as DH07, DH29, DL47, DL49, DL53. Naming is a community-style convention that spread through the field over time.

criteria.name: Density of promotional superlatives and hype vocabulary
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how heavily the abstract uses promotional vocabulary — remarkable, impressive, striking, significant, substantial, superior, novel, state-of-the-art, comprehensive, extensive. Count the promotional register, not whether the claims are true.
criteria.rationale: The V block already has v_kw_superlative and v_kw_novel; a judged version captures register rather than keyword hits. DL32 ('notable margins', 'practical efficacy'), DL45 ('state-of-the-art', 'great potential'), DH23 ('The results are striking') and DH21 all lean on it. Register is a writing-culture marker.

criteria.name: Famous benchmark and dataset name-dropping
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 by how many widely recognised benchmark or dataset names the abstract mentions (for example ImageNet, CIFAR, COCO, SuperGLUE, WMT, MNIST, LibriSpeech, Atari). Count recognisable names only; do not judge whether the evaluation is appropriate.
criteria.rationale: Deliberately the shallow, countable cousin of Track A's A04 (breadth of evaluation) — the routing audit should be able to tell them apart, and if it cannot, that is itself the result. DH28 (CIFAR-10, ImageNet, LSUN), DH03 (SuperGLUE), DH01 (IWSLT, WMT) versus DL42 and DL45 which name no canonical benchmark.

criteria.name: Signals of industrial-scale compute or frontier proprietary models
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract signals access to large-scale industrial resources: named proprietary frontier models used or compared against, explicit GPU counts or cluster scale, model sizes in billions of parameters, corpora at hundreds of millions of items. Score the resource signal only.
criteria.rationale: DH03 (PaLM, GPT-3), DH00 (340M images), DH05 ('8 A100 GPUs', 7B/13B/33B), DH08 (GPT-4o, GPT-o1, Llama), DH02 versus the resource-light DL31, DL43, DL47, DL49, DL53. Access to compute is an institutional attribute of the authors, not a property of the contribution — a textbook shortcut channel.

criteria.name: Applied-domain framing outside core machine learning
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how far the abstract is framed around an application domain outside core machine learning — medicine and clinical imaging, neuroscience and brain-computer interfaces, ecology and environment, field robotics, materials. Score domain framing only; core-ML work scores 0 regardless of quality.
criteria.rationale: A second topic marker, orthogonal to B05. DL38 (EEG/BCI), DL41 (medical image sequences), DL35 (ecological challenges), DL54 (sEEG brain-to-speech), DH13 (planetary rover navigation) cluster on one side of the slice. Domain fit to a venue's audience is a venue property, not a quality property.
